the program ORPHE US correctly predicts the complete sets of protein-coding and non-coding genes in the genomes of B.subtili and E.coli and accurately identifies the start of protein-coding gene fragments in the analyzed genomes.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ORPHEUS is an excellent gene finder, which is particularly useful for the analysis of bacterial genomes.
ORPHEUS predicts gene starts with an accuracy of about 90%, and gene starts are predicted with a higher accuracy than gene fragments.
the new program ORPHERUS is able to correctly identify 93-98% of genes longer than a hundred codons in completely sequenced genomes and to predict their starts with an accuracy of 83-96%.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a program that combines different evidence and achieves a high accuracy for gene prediction in bacterial genomes.
ORPHEUS predicts the correct gene start for 94% of genes in E.coli and 90% in B.subtilis.
ORPHEUS correctly predicts about 90% of all protein-coding genes and about 80% of their starts.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a combination of diverse evidence, such as similarity searches, statistical analysis of gene fragments, and ribosome-binding site predictions, is essential for accurate identification of gene starts in bacterial genomes.
gene recognition in completely-sequenced bacterial genomes can be done with a high degree of accuracy and confidence.
the use of multiple sources of evidence, in particular, the analysis of the statistical properties of ribosome binding sites, can improve the gene recognition accuracy in bacterial genomes.
